context: Short term: add the missing parts to anonymization_specs.yaml and add a test asserting the two lists are consistent (or that one derives from the other). Better: have both consume ONE source of truth rather than keeping two lists in sync by discipline - see the wider RCA on credential egress before choosing, because a second sync'd list is still a name-matching list.
description: Two independent secret-key lists must agree and do not. benchbox/core/results/platform_options.py:20 _SECRET_KEY_PARTS contains 'keyid' (added by PR #1346); benchbox/core/results/anonymization_specs.yaml secret_key_parts does NOT. anonymization.py:36 loads that spec and anonymization.py:360 _is_secret_metadata_key() matches against it, so the PUBLIC/anonymized export path - the one that produces published results - still exports s3_key_id and kms_key_id in clear. Evaluated 2026-07-30 against the live logic: s3_key_id False, kms_key_id False, aws_access_key_id True, pg_password True, username False. So PR #1346 fixed the internal metadata path and left the public path exposed, which is the more consequential of the two. No test asserts the two lists agree.
